enhanced.fullText:
The Higher Education Act's Textbook Information Requirements, codified under 20 U.S.C. § 1015b(d)-(e), mandate comprehensive disclosure of course materials and pricing information by higher education institutions receiving federal financial aid. This provision, enacted through the Higher Education Opportunity Act of 2008 (Public Law No. 110-315), addresses rising textbook costs by enhancing transparency and promoting informed student purchasing decisions.

Under 20 U.S.C. § 1015b(d)(1), institutions must disclose specific textbook information on internet course schedules used for preregistration and registration. Required disclosures include the International Standard Book Number (ISBN) and retail price information for all required and recommended textbooks and supplemental materials for each listed course. When ISBNs are unavailable, institutions must provide the textbook's author, title, publisher, and copyright date per 20 U.S.C. § 1015b(d)(2). The statute permits 'to be determined' designations only when disclosure is impractical for specific texts, with written course schedules directing students to web-based information sources.

The complementary bookstore information provision under 20 U.S.C. § 1015b(e) requires institutions to furnish campus bookstores with comprehensive course data as soon as practicable. This includes accurate course schedule information, textbook requirements, current enrollment numbers, and maximum enrollment capacity for each course or class section. These requirements facilitate bookstore inventory planning and support competitive pricing strategies.

Scope and applicability extend to all Title IV-eligible institutions, including public, private non-profit, and proprietary institutions participating in federal student aid programs. The Department of Education oversees compliance through institutional program reviews and complaint investigations, with potential penalties including loss of Title IV eligibility for persistent non-compliance.

The statute encourages institutions to disseminate information regarding cost-saving alternatives including book rental programs, used textbook availability, buyback initiatives, and alternative content delivery methods under 20 U.S.C. § 1015b(f). Recent enforcement guidance emphasizes proactive disclosure timelines, requiring information availability before registration periods commence to maximize student benefit from comparative shopping opportunities.
enhanced.summary: The Higher Education Act requires institutions to disclose ISBN numbers, retail prices, and detailed information for required and recommended textbooks on course schedules, while providing comprehensive course and enrollment data to campus bookstores.
enhanced.requirements:
## Course Schedule Disclosure Requirements
- Display ISBN and retail price for all required and recommended textbooks on internet course schedules used for preregistration
- Provide author, title, publisher, and copyright date when ISBN unavailable
- Designate 'to be determined' only when disclosure impractical for specific materials
- Include supplemental materials pricing in all course listings

## Bookstore Information Sharing
- Furnish campus bookstores with accurate course schedule information as soon as practicable
- Provide current student enrollment numbers and maximum enrollment capacity for each course
- Share textbook and supplemental material requirements for inventory planning

## Cost-Saving Information Dissemination
- Promote awareness of book rental programs and used textbook availability
- Communicate buyback program details and alternative delivery options
- Ensure written course schedules reference web-based textbook information locations
enhanced.reportingRequirements: No specific federal reporting deadlines mandated; institutions must ensure textbook information availability before each registration period commences. Compliance monitored through Department of Education program reviews and student complaint processes.
